subtopics.name: Physical Quantities and SI Units
objectives: Distinguish between fundamental and derived quantities.
State and use SI units for common physical quantities.
Convert between units and use standard form.

subtopics.name: Measurement Techniques and Errors
objectives: Describe the correct use of measuring instruments (vernier caliper, micrometer, etc.).
Distinguish between systematic and random errors.
Calculate absolute, relative, and percentage errors.

subtopics.name: Dimensional Analysis
objectives: Determine dimensions of derived quantities.
Use dimensional analysis to verify equations.
Check homogeneity of physical equations.

subtopics.name: Scalar and Vector Quantities
objectives: Distinguish between scalar and vector quantities.
Give examples of scalars (speed, mass) and vectors (velocity, force).
Represent vectors graphically using arrows.

subtopics.name: Vector Addition and Resolution
objectives: Add vectors using the triangle and parallelogram laws.
Resolve a vector into horizontal and vertical components.
Calculate the resultant of two or more vectors.

subtopics.name: Types of Motion and Equations
objectives: Apply the equations of uniformly accelerated motion.
Distinguish between linear, circular, oscillatory, and random motion.
Solve problems involving displacement, velocity, and acceleration.

subtopics.name: Motion Graphs
objectives: Interpret displacement-time and velocity-time graphs.
Calculate acceleration and displacement from motion graphs.
Describe the motion of a body from its graph.

subtopics.name: Projectile Motion
objectives: Calculate range, maximum height, and time of flight of a projectile.
Resolve projectile motion into horizontal and vertical components.
Explain the trajectory of a projectile under gravity.

subtopics.name: Newton's Laws of Motion
objectives: State and apply Newton's three laws of motion.
Calculate force using F = ma.
Describe inertia and its relationship to mass.

subtopics.name: Momentum and Impulse
objectives: Define linear momentum and impulse.
Apply conservation of linear momentum.
Distinguish between elastic and inelastic collisions.

subtopics.name: Conditions for Equilibrium
objectives: State the conditions for static equilibrium (sum of forces = 0, sum of torques = 0).
Calculate moments and torques about a point.
Solve problems involving levers, beams, and balanced forces.

subtopics.name: Work and Energy
objectives: Define work done and calculate it using W = Fd cos(theta).
Distinguish between kinetic and potential energy.
Calculate changes in kinetic and potential energy.

subtopics.name: Conservation of Energy and Power
objectives: Apply the principle of conservation of mechanical energy.
Define power and calculate it using P = W/t and P = Fv.
Calculate efficiency of machines and systems.

subtopics.name: Types and Laws of Friction
objectives: Distinguish between static and kinetic friction.
State the laws of friction.
Calculate frictional force using f = mu*N.

subtopics.name: Effects of Friction
objectives: Describe advantages and disadvantages of friction.
Explain methods of reducing and increasing friction.
Apply friction concepts to inclined plane problems.

subtopics.name: Types of Simple Machines
objectives: Classify and describe levers, pulleys, inclined planes, gears, and screws.
Calculate mechanical advantage and velocity ratio.
Explain the relationship between MA, VR, and efficiency.

subtopics.name: Applications of Simple Machines
objectives: Solve problems involving pulleys and wheel-and-axle systems.
Calculate work done and efficiency for a given machine.
Explain how machines multiply force or speed.

subtopics.name: Hooke's Law and Elastic Properties
objectives: State Hooke's law and identify the elastic limit.
Calculate spring constant from force-extension graphs.
Distinguish between elastic and plastic deformation.

subtopics.name: Stress, Strain, and Young's Modulus
objectives: Define stress, strain, and Young's modulus.
Calculate Young's modulus from experimental data.
Compare elastic properties of different materials.

subtopics.name: Pressure in Solids and Fluids
objectives: Define pressure and calculate it using P = F/A.
Derive and apply the formula for pressure in a liquid (P = rho*g*h).
State and apply Pascal's principle.

subtopics.name: Atmospheric Pressure and Gas Pressure
objectives: Explain atmospheric pressure and describe how it is measured.
Describe the operation of a mercury barometer and manometer.
Explain how altitude affects atmospheric pressure.

subtopics.name: Archimedes' Principle and Buoyancy
objectives: State Archimedes' principle and apply it to problems.
Calculate upthrust on a submerged object.
Explain the conditions for floating and sinking.

subtopics.name: Surface Tension and Viscosity
objectives: Describe surface tension phenomena (meniscus, capillary rise).
Define viscosity and give examples of its effects.
Explain the effect of temperature on viscosity.

subtopics.name: Temperature Scales and Fixed Points
objectives: Define temperature and state the fixed points of common scales.
Convert between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin scales.
Explain the concept of absolute zero and the Kelvin scale.

subtopics.name: Types of Thermometers
objectives: Describe the working principles of liquid-in-glass, thermocouple, and resistance thermometers.
Compare the properties of different thermometric substances.
Select appropriate thermometers for different situations.

subtopics.name: Linear, Area, and Volume Expansion
objectives: Explain thermal expansion of solids, liquids, and gases.
Calculate linear, area, and volume expansivities.
Solve problems using expansion formulae.

subtopics.name: Applications of Thermal Expansion
objectives: Describe practical applications: bimetallic strip, thermostats, railway gaps.
Explain the anomalous expansion of water.
Discuss consequences of thermal expansion in engineering.

subtopics.name: Conduction and Convection
objectives: Explain heat conduction in terms of molecular vibration and free electrons.
Describe convection currents in fluids.
Compare thermal conductivities of different materials.

subtopics.name: Radiation and Applications
objectives: Describe infrared radiation and its properties.
Apply Stefan-Boltzmann law and Newton's law of cooling.
Explain heat loss in buildings and the greenhouse effect.

subtopics.name: Boyle's and Charles's Laws
objectives: State Boyle's law and apply it to calculate pressure-volume changes.
State Charles's law and apply it to calculate volume-temperature changes.
State the pressure law and solve related problems.

subtopics.name: Ideal Gas Equation
objectives: Derive and use the general gas equation PV/T = constant.
Apply PV = nRT in calculations.
Explain the concept of absolute zero from gas law graphs.

subtopics.name: Specific Heat Capacity
objectives: Define specific heat capacity and use Q = mcDeltaT.
Calculate heat exchange in calorimetry experiments.
Compare heat capacities of different substances.

subtopics.name: Latent Heat and Change of State
objectives: Define specific latent heat of fusion and vaporization.
Calculate heat absorbed or released during change of state.
Interpret heating and cooling curves.

subtopics.name: Wave Properties and Types
objectives: Describe transverse and longitudinal waves with examples.
Define amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period, and wave speed.
Apply the wave equation v = f*lambda.

subtopics.name: Wave Behaviour
objectives: Explain reflection, refraction, diffraction, and superposition.
Describe constructive and destructive interference.
Explain the formation of standing waves.

subtopics.name: Properties and Propagation of Sound
objectives: Explain that sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave.
Describe factors affecting speed of sound in different media.
Calculate frequency, wavelength, and speed of sound.

subtopics.name: Resonance and Musical Sounds
objectives: Explain resonance and describe experiments to demonstrate it.
Calculate frequencies of harmonics in open and closed pipes.
Distinguish between pitch, loudness, and quality of sound.

subtopics.name: Nature and Propagation of Light
objectives: State that light travels in straight lines and calculate shadow lengths.
Describe pinhole camera formation and calculate image size.
Explain the speed of light and its measurement.

subtopics.name: Photometry
objectives: Define luminous intensity and illuminance.
Apply the inverse square law for illuminance.
Solve problems involving candela and lux.

subtopics.name: Plane Mirror Reflection
objectives: State the laws of reflection.
Locate images formed by plane mirrors.
Describe image characteristics in a plane mirror.

subtopics.name: Curved Mirror Reflection
objectives: Define principal focus, focal length, and radius of curvature for curved mirrors.
Use the mirror formula (1/f = 1/u + 1/v) to locate images.
Describe applications of concave and convex mirrors.

subtopics.name: Snell's Law and Refractive Index
objectives: State Snell's law and calculate refractive index.
Explain total internal reflection and critical angle.
Describe applications of total internal reflection (optical fibres, prisms).

subtopics.name: Lenses and Optical Instruments
objectives: Distinguish between converging and diverging lenses.
Use the lens formula (1/f = 1/u + 1/v) and lens maker's equation.
Describe construction of microscopes, telescopes, and cameras.

subtopics.name: Dispersion and the Spectrum
objectives: Explain dispersion using a prism and relate it to refractive index variation.
Identify the colours of the visible spectrum and their order.
Explain the formation of a rainbow.

subtopics.name: Colour Mixing and Filters
objectives: Describe additive and subtractive colour mixing.
Explain primary, secondary, and complementary colours.
Describe the effect of colour filters on light.

subtopics.name: Electric Charges and Coulomb's Law
objectives: Describe methods of charging bodies (friction, induction, contact).
State and apply Coulomb's law.
Describe the distribution of charge on conductors.

subtopics.name: Electric Field and Potential
objectives: Define electric field strength and draw field line patterns.
Define electric potential and potential difference.
Calculate work done in moving a charge in an electric field.

subtopics.name: Capacitance and Capacitors
objectives: Define capacitance and calculate it using C = Q/V.
Calculate combined capacitance for series and parallel circuits.
Calculate energy stored in a capacitor.

subtopics.name: Ohm's Law and Resistance
objectives: State Ohm's law and identify ohmic and non-ohmic conductors.
Calculate resistance using V = IR.
Determine combined resistance for series and parallel circuits.

subtopics.name: EMF, Internal Resistance, and Power
objectives: Define EMF and terminal voltage.
Calculate current and voltage in circuits with internal resistance.
Calculate electrical power and energy using P = IV, P = I^2R, P = V^2/R.

subtopics.name: Kirchhoff's Laws
objectives: State and apply Kirchhoff's current law (junction rule).
State and apply Kirchhoff's voltage law (loop rule).
Solve multi-loop circuit problems.

subtopics.name: Magnetic Fields and Properties
objectives: Describe properties of magnets and magnetic materials.
Draw magnetic field patterns for bar magnets and current-carrying conductors.
Explain the domain theory of magnetism.

subtopics.name: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
objectives: State and apply Fleming's left-hand rule.
Calculate force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
Describe the working principle of a DC motor.

subtopics.name: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
objectives: State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.
Apply Lenz's law to determine direction of induced current.
Calculate induced EMF using E = N*dPhi/dt.

subtopics.name: Transformers and Generators
objectives: Describe the structure and working principle of a transformer.
Apply the turns ratio equation for transformers.
Explain the working principle of an AC generator and DC generator.

subtopics.name: AC Quantities and Rectification
objectives: Distinguish between peak and RMS values of AC voltage and current.
Explain half-wave and full-wave rectification using diodes.
Describe smoothing of rectified AC using capacitors.

subtopics.name: Reactance and Resonance
objectives: Define capacitive and inductive reactance.
Calculate impedance in RLC circuits.
Explain resonance in series RLC circuits and state the resonant frequency.

subtopics.name: Atomic Structure and Models
objectives: Describe Rutherford's scattering experiment and its conclusions.
Explain Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom.
Explain line emission spectra in terms of electron energy levels.

subtopics.name: Radioactivity and Nuclear Reactions
objectives: Describe properties of alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.
Write and balance nuclear equations.
Apply radioactive decay law and calculate half-life.

subtopics.name: Nuclear Fission and Fusion
objectives: Distinguish between nuclear fission and fusion.
Explain mass defect and binding energy using E = mc^2.
Describe applications and hazards of nuclear energy.

subtopics.name: Photoelectric Effect and Quantum Theory
objectives: Explain the photoelectric effect and its implications for quantum theory.
Use E = hf to calculate photon energy.
Explain threshold frequency and work function.

subtopics.name: Wave-Particle Duality and Semiconductors
objectives: Explain de Broglie's hypothesis of matter waves.
Describe p-type and n-type semiconductors.
Explain the working of a p-n junction diode and transistor.
